title: FAA Part 107 airspace practice questions
description: Free FAA Part 107 airspace practice questions on 14 CFR 107.41-107.47 and airspace classes. Every answer is explained and linked to its source.

questions.question: For Class E airspace, which portion does 107.41 include in its requirement for prior authorization from Air Traffic Control (ATC)?

options.A: All Class E airspace that begins at 1,200 feet AGL
options.B: The lateral boundaries of the surface area of Class E airspace designated for an airport
options.C: Only Class E airspace above 14,500 feet MSL
options.D: Only Class E airspace along Federal Airways

questions.explanation: 107.41: "No person may operate a small unmanned aircraft in Class B, Class C, or Class D airspace or within the lateral boundaries of the surface area of Class E airspace designated for an airport unless that person has prior authorization from Air Traffic Control (ATC)."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.41, Operation in certain airspace (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which of the airspace rules in 107.41 through 107.47 does 107.205 list as one a certificate of waiver may authorize a deviation from?

options.A: 107.43, Operation in the vicinity of airports
options.B: 107.45, Operation in prohibited or restricted areas
options.C: 107.41, Operation in certain airspace
options.D: 107.47, Flight restrictions in the proximity of certain areas designated by notice to airmen

questions.explanation: 107.205 says a certificate of waiver "may authorize a deviation from the following regulations of this part", and its list includes "Section 107.41—Operation in certain airspace." Sections 107.43, 107.45 and 107.47 are not on that list.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.205, List of regulations subject to waiver (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.topic: Class E, Class G and the Class A floor
questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what does designating a large amount of the airspace over the United States as Class E airspace provide?

options.A: Airspace reserved for military training routes only
options.B: Airspace in which no ATC service is provided
options.C: Airspace closed to all unmanned aircraft
options.D: Sufficient airspace for the safe control and separation of aircraft during IFR operations

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "A large amount of the airspace over the United States is designated as Class E airspace. This provides sufficient airspace for the safe control and separation of aircraft during IFR operations."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: What does 107.43 prohibit?

options.A: Operating a small unmanned aircraft in a manner that interferes with operations and traffic patterns at any airport, heliport, or seaplane base
options.B: Operating a small unmanned aircraft from any airport property
options.C: Operating a small unmanned aircraft while an airport's control tower is closed
options.D: Operating a small unmanned aircraft over any public-use runway

questions.explanation: 107.43: "No person may operate a small unmanned aircraft in a manner that interferes with operations and traffic patterns at any airport, heliport, or seaplane base."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.43, Operation in the vicinity of airports (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what do the primary airport(s) within a terminal radar service area (TRSA) become?

options.A: Class B airspace
options.B: Class D airspace
options.C: Class G airspace
options.D: A restricted area

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "The primary airport(s) within the TRSA become(s) Class D airspace."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: 107.45 names two kinds of areas in which no person may operate a small unmanned aircraft unless that person has permission from the using or controlling agency. Which two?

options.A: Warning areas and alert areas
options.B: Military operations areas and controlled firing areas
options.C: Prohibited or restricted areas
options.D: Military training routes and parachute jump areas

questions.explanation: 107.45: "No person may operate a small unmanned aircraft in prohibited or restricted areas unless that person has permission from the using or controlling agency, as appropriate."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.45, Operation in prohibited or restricted areas (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which provisions does 107.47 require a person acting as remote pilot in command to comply with?

options.A: §§ 91.137 through 91.145 and 99.7 of 14 CFR
options.B: §§ 91.103 and 91.111 of 14 CFR only
options.C: Part 89 of 14 CFR only

questions.explanation: 107.47: "A person acting as a remote pilot in command must comply with the provisions of §§ 91.137 through 91.145 and 99.7 of this chapter."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.47, Flight restrictions in the proximity of certain areas designated by notice to airmen (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, which factors dictate the categories and types of airspace?

options.A: The weight and size of the aircraft that use the airspace only
options.B: The number of airports in each state
options.C: The type of radio each aircraft carries
options.D: The complexity or density of aircraft movements, nature of the operations conducted, the level of safety required, and national and public interest

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "The categories and types of airspace are dictated by the complexity or density of aircraft movements, nature of the operations conducted within the airspace, the level of safety required, and national and public interest."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: Which four types of airspace does the Study Guide list within the two airspace categories?

options.A: Controlled, uncontrolled, special use, and other airspace
options.B: Class A, Class B, Class C and Class D
options.C: Terminal, en route, oceanic and polar
options.D: Low, medium, high and very high altitude

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "there are four types: controlled, uncontrolled, special use, and other airspace."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.topic: Class B, C and D airspace
questions.question: How does the Study Guide describe the configuration of each Class B airspace area?

options.A: A single cylinder with a five nautical mile radius
options.B: A surface area only, with no layers above it
options.C: Individually tailored, consisting of a surface area and two or more layers
options.D: A ring from 1,200 feet AGL to 18,000 feet MSL, with no surface area

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "The configuration of each Class B airspace area is individually tailored, consists of a surface area and two or more layers" and is designed to contain all published instrument procedures once an aircraft enters the airspace.

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.topic: Class B, C and D airspace
questions.question: According to the Study Guide, which airports does Class C airspace generally surround?

options.A: Airports with no control tower and no radar service
options.B: Airports that have an operational control tower, are serviced by a radar approach control, and have a certain number of IFR operations or passenger enplanements
options.C: Airports served only by a UNICOM station
options.D: Airports with no radar approach control, whatever their traffic

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says Class C airspace surrounds "those airports that have an operational control tower, are serviced by a radar approach control, and have a certain number of instrument flight rules (IFR) operations or passenger enplanements."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.topic: Class B, C and D airspace
questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what may arrival extensions for instrument approach procedures (IAPs) be?

options.A: Class D or Class E airspace
options.B: Class A airspace
options.C: Prohibited areas
options.D: Class B airspace only

questions.explanation: The Study Guide, describing Class D airspace: "Arrival extensions for instrument approach procedures (IAPs) may be Class D or Class E airspace."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.topic: Class B, C and D airspace
questions.question: According to the Study Guide, when instrument procedures are published for an airport with Class D airspace, how is that airspace normally designed?

options.A: To leave the instrument approach paths outside the Class D area
options.B: As a single ring with a 30 NM radius
options.C: To extend upward to 18,000 feet MSL
options.D: To contain the procedures

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "The configuration of each Class D airspace area is individually tailored and, when instrument procedures are published, the airspace is normally designed to contain the procedures."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.topic: Class E, Class G and the Class A floor
questions.question: Which locations of Class E airspace does the Study Guide say sectional and other charts depict?

options.A: Only Class E airspace that begins at the surface
options.B: None; Class E airspace is described only in the AIM
options.C: All locations of Class E airspace with bases below 14,500 feet MSL
options.D: Only Class E airspace above FL 600

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "Sectional and other charts depict all locations of Class E airspace with bases below 14,500 feet MSL."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.topic: Class E, Class G and the Class A floor
questions.question: According to the Study Guide, up to what boundary does Class G airspace extend from the surface?

options.A: 18,000 feet MSL
options.B: The base of the overlying Class E airspace
options.C: 400 feet AGL
options.D: FL 600

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "Class G airspace extends from the surface to the base of the overlying Class E airspace."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, how is a prohibited area charted?

options.A: As an "R" followed by a number
options.B: As a "P" followed by a number (e.g., P-40)
options.C: As a "W" followed by a number
options.D: By name only, without a number

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "The area is charted as a "P" followed by a number (e.g., P-40)."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, over which waters may a warning area be located?

options.A: Only over inland lakes
options.B: Only over international waters
options.C: Only over land within the United States
options.D: Over domestic or international waters or both

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: a warning area is airspace "extending from 3 NM outward from the coast of the United States", and "A warning area may be located over domestic or international waters or both."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: Why does the Study Guide say there is no need to chart controlled firing areas (CFAs)?

options.A: They are active only at night
options.B: They always lie inside restricted areas
options.C: They do not cause a nonparticipating aircraft to change its flight path
options.D: They are listed only in the Chart Supplement U.S.

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "There is no need to chart CFAs since they do not cause a nonparticipating aircraft to change its flight path." Activities in a CFA "must be suspended" when an aircraft might be approaching the area.

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, with what phrase does the NOTAM that designates a temporary flight restriction (TFR) begin?

options.A: FLIGHT RESTRICTIONS
options.B: AIRSPACE CLOSED
options.C: SPECIAL NOTICE
options.D: NO FLY ZONE

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "The NOTAM begins with the phrase “FLIGHT RESTRICTIONS” followed by the location of the temporary restriction, effective time period, area defined in statute miles, and altitudes affected."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what are military training routes (MTRs) used for?

options.A: Arrivals and departures of air carriers at Class B airports
options.B: Long-range small unmanned aircraft delivery flights
options.C: FAA flight checks of navigation aids
options.D: Military aircraft maintaining proficiency in tactical flying

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "MTRs are routes used by military aircraft to maintain proficiency in tactical flying."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)
